entities.name: Peroz I Kushanshah
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Peroz I Kushanshah was the Kushanshah of the Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom from 245 to 275 CE, succeeding Ardashir I Kushanshah.

He was a key figure in the expansion of the Kushano-Sasanian Empire into western territories, further pushing the weakened Kushan Empire to Mathura in North India.

Under his rule, the Kushano-Sasanians minted coins in Balkh, Herat, and Gandhara, showcasing their extensive control over the region.

Peroz I Kushanshah's energetic leadership and military campaigns significantly expanded the empire's borders, leaving a lasting legacy in the history of the ancient world.

The Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom's expansion under Peroz I Kushanshah had far-reaching consequences, influencing the political and cultural landscape of the region for centuries to come.

This remarkable leader's impact on the ancient world is still studied and debated by historians today, offering valuable insights into the complexities of regional politics and cultural exchange.

Peroz I Kushanshah's name is etched in the annals of history, symbolizing the enduring power of the Kushano-Sasanian Empire and its significance in shaping the ancient world.
